news_title: Product safety recall - 1 308 units of Schneider electric SYBTU1 and SYBTU2 battery modules - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recall - 1 308 units of Schneider electric SYBTU1 and SYBTU2 battery modules - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – 1 308 units of Schneider electric SYBTU1 and SYBTU2 battery modules
Date Posted:
November 25, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) informs consumers about the recall of certain Schneider Electric SYBTU1 and SYBTU2 battery modules used in Symmetra PX, Smart UPS VT and Galaxy 3500 Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems, as notified by Schneider Electric South Africa.
The affected battery modules can be identified by the following model numbers: SYBTU1-PLP, SYBTHU1-PLP, SYBTU2-PLP and SYBTU2-PLPLL. The affected units have serial numbers starting with “5D” and were made available for sale between September 2024 and October 2025.
According to Schneider Electric, the recall is due to inadequate grounding of the battery module enclosure, which may create an electric shock hazard under fault conditions. A total of 1 308 battery modules is affected. The products were supplied directly to Schneider Electric’s business customers and are used in large industrial and commercial applications.
Customers who own the affected battery modules should check the model and serial numbers, then contact Schneider Electric to arrange an inspection and any necessary corrective action.
Questions relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.
Ends

efet_title: Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall
Date Posted:
October 3, 2024
On 16 September 2024, Shoprite Checkers notified the Consumer Commission (NCC) of a product recall of the Deli Hummus range manufactured by BM Foods (a member of Sea Harvest Group), following the detection of Listeria Monocytogenes which is a species of foodborne bacteria.
The affected products are the Deli Hummus range, specifically the following:
Traditional Hummus (125g and 300g);
Reduced Fat Hummus (125g);
Zataar Hummus (125g and 300g);
Red Pepper Hummus (125g and 300g); and
Caramelised Onion Hummus (125g).
The respective sell-by dates of the products are 10 September 2024 to 08 October 2024.
Subsequent to the product recall notification, and in line with Section 60 of the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008, Shoprite Checkers has now provided an interim Investigation Report to the NCC on the Deli Hummus range. The preliminary findings of the report point to some areas of concern on product handling at the manufacturing level, however, the NCC awaits a final report from Shoprite Checkers. Parallel to the said in-house processes, the NCC is independently investigating the recalled products on identified operational issues that pertain to food safety.
The NCC’s Acting Commissioner, Mr. Hardin Ratshisusu, urged consumers to immediately stop consuming the products and return same to the supplier for a full refund with or without any proof of purchase. He further added that “at this stage, the NCC is not able to determine the extent of the distribution of the products as this is the subject of an investigation. Suppliers are urged not to distribute these products further until the investigation is finalised.”
The NCC is monitoring this recall based on the Product Recall provisions of the Consumer Protection Action read with the product recall safety guidelines.
ENDS
Issued by: National Consumer Commission (NCC)

news_title: Product safety recall – 67 Junior Lemieux Equestrian Riding Stirrups - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recall - 67 Junior Lemieux Equestrian Riding Stirrups - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – 67 Junior Lemieux Equestrian Riding Stirrups
Date Posted:
November 17, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) informs consumers about the recall of 67 LeMieux Junior Vector Balance Stirrups, as notified by LeMieux.
The affected stirrups are available in aluminium, black and rose gold, and have the following product codes: 5063240053026, 5063240053033 and 5063240080114. The model numbers are IT05553, IT05554 and IT06371.
According to LeMieux, the recall follows customer reports that the stirrup can catch a rider’s boot during a fall. The raised edge next to the release arm, together with the size of the foot opening, may prevent the rider’s foot from coming free, even when the release arm has opened. This could result in injury to the rider. The affected stirrups were sold in South Africa between February 2025 and November 2026 through The Western Shoppe (Pty) Ltd and Unicorn Tack.
Consumers who have purchased the affected product are advised to stop using it immediately and return it to the point of purchase for a full refund.
Questions and queries relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.

news_title: Product safety recalls – UD Trucks and Honda motorcycles - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recalls - UD Trucks and Honda motorcycles - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recalls – UD Trucks and Honda motorcycles
Date Posted:
November 16, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) notifies consumers about the recalls of certain UD Trucks and Honda motorcycles, as reported by the respective suppliers.
UD TRUCKS – 40 VEHICLES
UD Trucks Southern Africa notified the NCC that it is recalling 40 (forty) certain extra-heavy commercial vehicles. The trucks were sold in South Africa from 23 October 2026 to 31 October 2027. The recall is due to a defect requiring a software update to the electrical switch panel. According to the supplier, the flexible switch may fail to switch on, potentially affecting its operation.
HONDA MOTORCYCLES – 51 MOTORCYCLES
Honda Motor Southern Africa (Pty) Ltd informed the NCC that it is recalling 51 (fifty-one) Honda CRF250RS, CRF250RXS, CRF450RS and CRF450RXS 25YM motorcycles. The recall affects motorcycles sold between 2025 and 2026 nationally through the Honda dealer network. According to the supplier, the affected motorcycles have a handlebar under-holder machining defect. When an external force exceeding the holding force is applied to the handlebar pipe by an impact during use, the handlebar pipe can move and, in the worst case, cause the rider to fall.
Consumers who own the affected vehicles and motorcycles are advised to contact their nearest authorised dealership to arrange for the replacement or software update at no cost to the customer.
Questions and queries relating to this recall may be directed to: ProductRecall@thencc.org.za.
Ends
